scope: Independent read-only M14-03-05 perf shared ownership review. No candidate, execution, source flag release or acceptance.

actual_source_fragments.fact: Shared descriptor find unlocks before returning its raw descriptor. A callback-local pin occurs after this escape.
Ordinary close unlinks under process mckfd_lock P, then close_cb and free execute after unlock, before forwarding host close.
Group read walks leader and sibling pointers and copies to user between list reads; live-event references alone do not stabilize concurrent list mutation.
Enable publishes raw Process.monitoring_event locally or under the found-process hash lock; stop/reset/refresh branches have distinct semantics.
Selected do_exit reloads proc, loads monitoring_event and invokes sync_child_event while retaining its existing process update-lock/IRQ/preemption ordering.
Selected do_fork dereferences the parent monitoring event attr and publishes the same pointer in child when inherit is set; both need a live owning/pinned edge.
Selected termination checks then separately reloads monitoring_event before sync_child_event; raw pointer validity is not established by non-null.
Selected scheduler reads next Process.monitoring_event repeatedly and performs reset/start; lifetime acquisition must fit its existing IRQ/scheduling context.
Selected PMI chooses descriptor under P, then reads only sig_no/fd after unlock and calls set_signal. Snapshotting those scalars under P is sufficient for this dereference boundary.
Fork copy holds only private child P, reads/copies parent descriptor and invokes copied dup callback. Parent storage/event ownership must be acquired before copy, not inside a later callback.
Failed fork drains copied descriptor nodes without close/dup undo; newly acquired managed ownership requires a matching explicit unwind.
Actual last-VM path already holds P while close_all calls close callbacks. A perf close callback cannot recursively acquire P or wait/offload there.
Final Process release frees main-thread pages before taking P and draining descriptor nodes; deferred counter teardown cannot rely on that Thread allocation remaining live.
Actual last Thread release destroys Thread before releasing VM. An event->Thread long-lived reference can retain VM->descriptor->event and form a retirement cycle.
Actual extra-register setter reads/writes current Thread allocation map, may select alternate register and reserves only on successful local claim; map release must consume the real claim.
Actual counter allocator only scans Thread.pmc_alloc_map; current open reserves the bit after host offload, so selection is not an exclusive reservation.

required_protocol_obligations.obligation: Only real perf publication/copy establishes managed kind, descriptor identity and generation. Acquire descriptor/event use ownership under P before returning from shared lookup; then drop P before callbacks. Resolve never casts arbitrary data from signalfd/XPMEM or treats callback-address equality as an already-established kind. Every actual free/unpublish/copy path must preserve or retire that identity exactly once.

Pin the actual group-fd event before unlock, preserve the existing accepted group-fd domain and stabilize leader/member topology for all traversals. Pending open owns its event, group reference/link contribution and exclusive counter reservation across unlocked host offload. Error unwind removes only its own link/count/mask/reservation and event; a post-host-success failure must close the real host fd. No whole prior-mask restore that can erase concurrent valid ownership.

Reserve under a real synchronized owner identity before other opens can select the same bit. Counter measurement count remains data. Track creator Thread identity and actual extra-register acquisitions independently of whichever thread closes. The real Thread destruction path must disconnect/retire the map owner before freeing it; late event retirement must not dereference a dead Thread. Do not introduce an event->Thread->VM->descriptor->event lifetime cycle.

Process.monitoring_event is a distinct owning edge, not a borrow protected by descriptor reference alone. Define synchronized publication/replacement/clear, reader pin acquisition and final detach for ioctl, inherited fork, scheduler reset/start, do_exit and terminate/sync-child. Pin before inherited attr dereference and child publication; unwind child ownership on failed clone. A bare load followed by refcount increment is not safe against concurrent final free.

A stable group traversal must remain valid through read/start/reset/stop/sync-child and concurrent close/open; protect mutable accounting/state consistently. Capture/pin any snapshot under its lock and release spinlocks before usercopy/offload. Do not hold a new registry spinlock through the existing full body merely because its root event was pinned.

Ordinary close removes visibility once, copied descriptors acquire actual parent-side ownership before copying, failed fork undoes acquired ownership, last-VM close is safe with P already held, and final descriptor drain cannot double-drop or free pinned storage. Any deferred destruction must have an actual drain trigger and keep every data owner it still accesses alive, without retaining the Thread/VM cycle. The new protocol must cover Linux numeric-fd close/reuse versus in-flight forwarded operations as well as pointer storage.

Define a total order compatible with existing P-held VM and copy routes. A possible proposal order is P then a new IRQ-safe registry lock R for brief resolve/mutation only, with no R-to-P acquisition, host request, usercopy, blocking wait or callbacks under R. Process-hash/update/runqueue/IRQ callers of monitoring operations must be included in the real lock graph; finalization occurs outside all relevant spinlocks or only enqueues a bounded retire record there. This is a required source proof, not an approved lock implementation.

minimum_actual_participants.responsibility: Perf open/validation/publish/group and all participating descriptor lookup read/ioctl/fcntl/mmap/close boundaries; typed callbacks, group/accounting traversals, monitoring publication/clear and selected do_exit reader.
Parent-protected copy, acquired-reference unwind, P-held VM close, final descriptor drain and real Thread destruction/map-owner retirement.
Real monitoring inheritance and failed-child ownership retirement.
Actual sync-child monitoring read pin and terminal detach.
Scheduler monitoring access and PMI scalar snapshot or otherwise genuine pre-unlock pin.
Actual counter/extra-register reservation and owner-map access; real hardware/IRQ contract remains required.
